thread:
Maya Li: Security team at BankZ says they won't sign PO until we confirm HSM handoff steps + cost for emergency hotpatch support. They specifically want: who holds signing key after handoff, how we verify patched artifacts offline, and whether model-only swaps are supported without full bundle replace.
Owen Park: Summary: we can do customer-HSM signing during handoff (we hand the artifact, they sign with their HSM, we record signature and cert). After handoff Redwood no longer signs that artifact. For POC we can offer a 'co-sign' flow where Redwood signs first and customer co-signs for verification.
Diego Ruiz: Model-only swaps: supported if model ABI compatible. Installer includes a patcher daemon that does atomic swap + symlink, with optional graceful reload. If ABI breaks -> full bundle replace.
Hannah Cole: Pricing ask from procurement: cost for co-signing handoff + 24/7 emergency delta patch SLA (<4h) during POC.
billing-bot: Estimate: co-sign handoff engineering + key ceremony support $10,000 one-time; POC emergency delta SLA $5,500/month (up to 4 incidents). Final needs finance OK.
Owen Park: Offline verification checklist for SOC (I will produce): verify signature (ed25519), check sha256, validate embedded SBOM hash, and inspect timestamp/certificate chain. Will include exact commands. Example: 
``n
redwood-verify --pubkey /opt/redwood/customer_pub.pem --file model.patch --sig model.patch.sig
sha256sum model.patch
cat sbom.json | jq .packages[0].name
```
Diego Ruiz: Note: in sealed/offline installs, the operator must pre-load the trust bundle (pubkeys & certs). The patcher rejects patches not signed by an allowed key. If verification fails we abort and keep current symlink - manual intervention required.
Hannah Cole: Contract language note: autonomous patch/rollback behavior must be in SOW. For Private installs we require customer signoff for auto-rollback or we'll mark as manual-only.
Maya Li: Customer question: can we provide a dry-run apply for patches so their SOC can test offline?
Owen Park: Yes - patcher supports --dry-run that performs verification and checksum checks and outputs a simulated plan, no swap performed. Example: 
``n
patcher apply --file model.patch --dry-run
```
Diego Ruiz: Ops constraints: USB handoff vs jumpbox transfer. If using USB, we require a signed manifest with timestamps and an event id. Runbook must include manual verification steps and the command to record event id.
ops-bot: Build: sealed-bundle v2.3-poc sha256:9f8e7d6c staged /artifacts/sealed/4995550000; patcher v0.9.
Maya Li: Action items: @Owen create one-page SOC checklist + sample commands (ETA 24h); @Diego draft runbook (USB handoff, dry-run, rollback steps) ETA 48h; @Hannah coordinate SOW clause with legal. I'll reply to BankZ with this plan and provisional pricing. :thumbsup:
